mission.name: Crossing - target near starboard beam
mission.description:
Target is nearly abeam on own-ship's starboard side (~90 deg relative). Own-ship must give way.

Additional, beyond the 22 Imazu problems: the abeam (~90 deg) point of the same starboard-crossing bearing sweep as UM03/UM04 -- Imazu problem 2 only samples one starboard bearing (~45 deg), never a full-abeam contact.
pass_criteria: Own-ship is give-way and passes astern of the target.
Minimum CPA stays above the safe-distance threshold.

violations: t=150s: own-ship cited Rule 15 and turned left (from 30° to 0°) while ts1 was still a crossing vessel on its starboard side -- violates Rule 15/Rule 16 because the give-way vessel must take early and substantial action to AVOID the target (normally to starboard, per Rule 8), and never alter course to port for a vessel on own-ship's port side (Rule 17 for stand-on would not apply here as own-ship was give-way); the COLREG-compliant action would have been to maintain the existing 30° starboard turn or turn further to starboard to pass astern of ts1.

t=300s: own-ship cited Rule 15 but the ground truth says Rule 13 applies because own-ship was overtaking ts1 from astern (rel_bearing=15deg, CPA=0.027NM, TCPA=7s) -- this is a fabricated/wrong citation; an overtaking vessel must keep clear of the overtaken vessel, typically by altering course to starboard to pass on the target's starboard side or maintaining a safe lateral separation, not by citing the crossing rule.

t=750s: own-ship cited Rule 15 and turned left (from 15° to 345°) but the ground truth says no rule applies (quiet -- CPA/TCPA too large for real risk of collision, rel_bearing=-101deg, CPA=0.637NM) -- this is a fabricated citation; when no risk of collision exists, no COLREG action rule applies, and the turn was unnecessary and incorrectly justified.

t=150s: own-ship cited Rule 15 and turned left (from 30° to 0°) while ts1 was still a crossing vessel on its starboard side -- violates Rule 15/Rule 16 because the give-way vessel must take early and substantial action to AVOID the target (normally to starboard, per Rule 8), and never alter course to port for a vessel on own-ship's port side (Rule 17 for stand-on would not apply here as own-ship was give-way); the COLREG-compliant action would have been to maintain the existing 30° starboard turn or turn further to starboard to pass astern of ts1.

t=300s: own-ship cited Rule 15 but the ground truth says Rule 13 applies because own-ship was overtaking ts1 from astern (rel_bearing=15deg, CPA=0.027NM, TCPA=7s) -- this is a fabricated/wrong citation; an overtaking vessel must keep clear of the overtaken vessel, typically by altering course to starboard to pass on the target's starboard side or maintaining a safe lateral separation, not by citing the crossing rule.

t=750s: own-ship cited Rule 15 and turned left (from 15° to 345°) but the ground truth says no rule applies (quiet -- CPA/TCPA too large for real risk of collision, rel_bearing=-101deg, CPA=0.637NM) -- this is a fabricated citation; when no risk of collision exists, no COLREG action rule applies, and the turn was unnecessary and incorrectly justified.
compliant_actions: t=0s: own-ship turned right (from 0° to 30°) -- correctly satisfies Rule 15/Rule 16 because ts1 was a crossing vessel on own-ship's starboard side (rel_bearing=90deg, CPA=0.000NM, TCPA=401s), making own-ship the give-way vessel required to take early and substantial action to avoid the target, and a starboard turn is the appropriate action.

t=450s: own-ship held course and speed -- correctly satisfies the requirement that no action is needed when no rule applies (ground truth: no rule applies, CPA=0.210NM, TCPA=0s, quiet -- CPA/TCPA too large for real risk of collision), and own-ship correctly cited 'none'.

t=600s: own-ship held course and speed -- correctly satisfies the requirement that no action is needed when no rule applies (ground truth: no rule applies, CPA=0.423NM, TCPA=0s, quiet -- CPA/TCPA too large for real risk of collision), and own-ship correctly cited 'none'.

t=900s: own-ship held course (turned left from 345° to 315°, but this was a course adjustment, not a collision-avoidance manoeuvre for ts1) -- correctly satisfies the requirement that no action is needed when no rule applies (ground truth: no rule applies, CPA=0.746NM, TCPA=0s, quiet -- CPA/TCPA too large for real risk of collision), and own-ship correctly cited 'none'.

params.system_prompt:
You are the navigator on a large commercial vessel. Decide the next helm order.

MISSION REQUIREMENTS -- this mission is only completed successfully if ALL of these hold, not just
the first one you happen to satisfy:
1. Every contact's CPA stays at or above this mission's safe passing distance (given further below)
   at all times -- exactly as mandatory as actually reaching the goal. There is no automatic safety
   net correcting your choice if you get this wrong: your own action each step is what the ship
   actually does.
2. Every manoeuvre you take while a real collision risk exists complies with COLREG.
3. You reach the mission goal.

PRIORITY ORDER when these pull in different directions -- always in this order, never reversed:
1. Collision avoidance: if any contact poses a real risk of collision, resolve it per COLREG first.
2. Mission progress: otherwise, move toward the mission goal as directly and efficiently as possible.

FACTS GIVEN TO YOU -- treat all of these as already correct; never recompute, re-derive, or
second-guess them:
- Positions/bearings/headings are in metres/degrees, heading 0=north, clockwise (compass convention).
- rel.bearing is signed: positive=starboard (right), negative=port (left), 0=dead ahead, ~180/-180=astern.
- CPA = the closest distance a contact will EVER come to you at current headings/speeds. TCPA = seconds
  until that closest point.
- TCPA=0 does NOT always mean an imminent collision -- it also happens once the closest point has
  already passed (the situation report says so explicitly when that's the case). Judge real risk from
  CPA alone, never from TCPA alone.
- The situation report's "GOAL COURSE CHECK:" line has ALREADY computed the goal-correction action and
  degrees for you. Never substitute a contact's rel.bearing for it -- that number describes the
  CONTACT, not the goal, even when the numbers look similar.

DECISION PROCEDURE -- follow in order:
1. Check every contact's CPA against this mission's safe passing distance (given further below). If
   none are below it, there is no real collision risk right now -- go to step 3.
2. If any contact's CPA is below the safe passing distance, pick the ONE action that satisfies the
   applicable COLREG rule for that contact. This step overrides everything below it.
3. Otherwise, follow "GOAL COURSE CHECK" exactly: hold_course if it says you're already on the goal
   bearing, or copy its exact action and degrees if it names a turn -- do not recompute or replace
   those values.
4. Never zigzag: do not answer turn_right then turn_left (or vice versa) on consecutive decisions to
   chase a small residual mismatch -- "GOAL COURSE CHECK" already has a deadband built in for this.
5. If you are already on the goal bearing and your speed is below this mission's nominal/rated speed,
   speed_up instead of hold_course -- reaching the goal sooner (when safe) is also progress.

Ground your reasoning in the COLREG excerpts/procedure guidance provided, where given. Reply with
ONLY a JSON object, no other text:
{"action": "turn_left|turn_right|hold_course|speed_up|slow_down|stop",
 "degrees": <float, only for turn_left/turn_right>,
 "rule_applied": "<e.g. Rule 15, or 'none' if no rule applies>",
 "reasoning": "<one or two sentences>"}
